title: 03:00 Watch Digest — annotated shift log and runbook notes
body:
Summary

0300-0600 UTC overnight watch. Low-severity user-facing impact: transient latency degradation for hosted-generations (p95 increased ~120ms above baseline for ~18 minutes). No customer data loss, no escalations to exec. Two active follow-ups created.

Pre-shift checklist (completed)
- Pager subscriptions: verified (pagerduty on-call verified for eu/night and apac-oncall).
- Metric snapshot: baseline p95=210ms, p99=690ms at start-of-shift. Token throughput steady at 38k tps.
- Autoscaler warm-up: confirmed pool sizes at configured min for dedicated clusters.
- KV-cache health: regional hit-rate 98% EU, 95% US.

Incidents and timeline
- 03:07 UTC — latency surge observed on hosted-api-route /v1/generate (route: redwood/gpt-13b-realtime). Alerts: latency-p95-up (threshold 300ms) fired.
  - Indicators: small spike in GPU queue depth on pool-dedicated-1, concurrent requests per worker increased from 20->38.
  - Immediate actions: scaled pool-dedicated-1 by +25% (manual override) at 03:09 UTC, enabled fallback policy to model-variant quantized-v2 at 03:10 UTC for new requests.
  - Observed effect: p95 returned to within 40ms of baseline by 03:15 UTC.
  - Root cause hypothesis: short-lived request fanout from a customer A/B test causing bursty KV cache cold-starts and per-worker queue saturation.
  - Ticket: JIRA SRE-4271 created 03:18 UTC (owner: Marco Alvarez).

- 04:12 UTC — minor error-rate increase on embedding endpoint (err 500 from model runtime) affecting 0.6% of requests for ~7 minutes.
  - Action: temporarily routed embedding requests to fallback region eu-2 at 04:14 UTC. Patch deployed to restart one host (infra/host-emb-03) at 04:20 UTC.
  - Post-mitigation: error rate back to baseline within 3 minutes of restart.
  - Follow-up: health-check tuning for embedding hosts (Sofia Chen).

Pages and escalations
- PagerDuty: singlepage to eng-oncall at 03:08 UTC; no escalation to on-call SME.
- Slack: #sre-ops notified, brief thread with timeline and mitigation commands (see linked PR for small autoscaler guard change).

Runbook observations / gaps
- Current "Scale-on-queue-depth" runbook assumes uniform request size; does not account for model-variant heterogeneity. During the event, manual scaling and model fallback were necessary because autoscaler thresholds did not trigger fast enough.
- Suggest adding a short procedure: "If per-worker concurrent requests >30 AND KV-miss-rate >2% -> temporary manual scale + enable model-variant fallback" with exact CLI commands.
- Embedding host restart procedure exists but lacks guidance on safe rolling restart when error spike originates from a single host. Add checklist to avoid cascading evictions.

Follow-ups and ownership
- SRE-4271 (owner: Marco Alvarez): investigate root-cause of burst source, reproduce with load test, propose autoscaler tuning. Due: 2026-04-28.
- RUNBOOK-UPDATE-12 (owner: Aisha Patel): add explicit fallback-and-scale recipe to scale-on-queue-depth runbook, include example kubectl/infractl commands and canary thresholds. Due: 2026-04-27.
- EMB-HEALTH-TUNE (owner: Sofia Chen): add host-level liveness/health-check improvements and safe-restart checklist. Due: 2026-05-02.

Commands executed (notes)
- infractl pools scale --pool pool-dedicated-1 --factor 1.25 --reason "latency surge 2026-04-25 03:09Z"
- infractl route set-fallback --route redwood/gpt-13b-realtime --variant quantized-v2 --allow-new-conns true
- ssh infra@host-emb-03 sudo systemctl restart model-runtime.service

Metrics snapshots (post-mitigation)
- p95 pre-incident: 210ms, during: 340ms, post: 250ms
- queue depth per-worker pre: 20, peak: 38, post: 22
- KV cache miss-rate US: 5.3% peak, EU: 2.1% peak

Notes for next shift
- Expect follow-up actions on autoscaler tuning and runbook edits. If you see repeat bursts from similar customer fingerprints, escalate to product-eng for coordination (ticket in SRE-4271).
- Keep an eye on embedding hosts: if host-emb-03 exhibits repeat failures, do a full host replacement and isolate from load balancer before rejoining.

Retrospective suggestions (short)
- Introduce a short synthetic workload that simulates heterogeneous request sizes to catch autoscaler gaps in pre-prod.
- Add a short post-incident checklist: capture sample request ids and a hashed client fingerprint to speed up product correlation.

Appendix: quick doc links and references
- Runbooks: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SRE/pages/987654321/Runbooks
- Infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/812 (autoscaler guard small change)
- Incident ticket: JIRA SRE-4271

End of shift note: handing over to Kenji — timestamp 06:00 UTC. Please ping in #sre-ops if anything degrades; I will be reachable for context until 09:00 UTC.
